experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass
experiences.description: Ski the legendary slopes of Zermatt with a full-day lift pass covering over 360km of groomed runs with iconic Matterhorn views. Book slopes near the village center to maximize ski-in/ski-out access from your hotel. Given late flight arrival on Day 1, begin skiing from Day 2 onwards to ensure you are well-rested. Stay in Zermatt village itself to eliminate transfer time and start skiing by 9am sharp.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Rail & Snow Experience
experiences.description: Take the cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Wengen directly to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, Europe's highest railway station. Explore the Ice Palace, walk the Plateau, and enjoy panoramic Alpine views. Stay in Grindelwald to be steps from the departure station, cutting commute time significantly and making a mid-morning departure ideal after a restful first night.

experiences.name: St. Moritz Snowkiting & Ice Activities on Lake St. Moritz
experiences.description: Experience world-class snowkiting, ice skating, and curling on the frozen Lake St. Moritz, a hub for winter sports enthusiasts. Lessons and equipment rentals are available directly on the lake. Book accommodation in St. Moritz town center to walk to the lake in under 10 minutes, avoiding costly and time-consuming transfers from outlying villages.
experiences.location: Lake St. Moritz, St. Moritz, Engadin Valley

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Off-Piste Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a certified mountain guide for a half-day off-piste freeride experience through Verbier's legendary backcountry terrain, including the famous Mont-Fort glacier area. Staying in Verbier village puts you within walking distance of the main gondola, allowing you to hit the slopes by 8:30am before crowds arrive. Schedule this mid-trip when legs are warmed up from earlier ski days.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trails
experiences.description: Explore over 100km of groomed Nordic and cross-country ski trails around Davos, the highest city in the Alps. Trails begin directly from the town promenade, making it effortless to step out from centrally located hotels and ski immediately. This is an ideal lower-intensity activity for Day 6 or 7 to wind down before departure, with no lift passes required and trails accessible all day.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Bernese Oberland accommodation (approx. 1.5-2 hours by train via Interlaken). Use Swiss Travel Pass or buy a point-to-point ticket for budget savings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Bernese Oberland Boutique Stay. Once settled, take a leisurely stroll through the nearby village to get oriented. Visit the local tourist office to pick up free maps, ski pass info, and any discount vouchers. Window shop and scout affordable ski rental shops for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village center on foot. Find a cozy local restaurant or mountain hut for a classic Swiss dinner. Rest early to recover from travel and prepare for active days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Grab a sandwich or pastry at the airport or train station café before/during travel (budget ~5-8 CHF).
meals.lunch: Pick up a baguette, cheese, and fruit from a Migros or Coop supermarket near the train station en route (budget ~8-12 CHF) — Switzerland's best budget hack.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local Bernese Oberland gasthaus or mountain restaurant. Try Rösti (Swiss potato dish) or a simple cheese fondue set. Look for 'Tagesteller' (daily special) which is typically the most affordable hot meal (~18-25 CHF).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a regional ski pass or Jungfrau ski region pass upon arrival if planning multiple ski days — multi-day passes offer significant savings. Download the SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) app for real-time train schedules. Confirm ski rental availability and book in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the nearest ski area in the Bernese Oberland (Grindelwald, Wengen, or Mürren). Rent ski equipment from a local shop — compare prices between village rental shops vs. resort-based ones as village shops are often 20-30% cheaper. Hit the slopes early (9:00 AM) to avoid crowds and make the most of your lift pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on beginner to intermediate runs. Take a break at a mid-mountain self-service restaurant for a warm drink and snack. Explore different pistes and enjoy the stunning views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Return equipment by 4:30 PM to avoid late fees.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Warm up with a hot shower and relax sore muscles. Head out for a budget dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the accommodation if breakfast is included. If not, grab yogurt, bread, and fruit from Coop or Migros supermarket (~5-8 CHF).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the supermarket (sandwiches, energy bars, hot thermos of tea/coffee) to eat on the mountain and avoid expensive on-mountain restaurant prices (~8-12 CHF).
meals.dinner: Try a local pizzeria or kebab shop in the village for an affordable hot meal (~15-20 CHF). Many Swiss mountain towns have surprisingly good affordable international options.

day_by_day.notes: Ski rental for a full day typically costs 35-55 CHF. A regional lift pass for one day is approximately 60-80 CHF. Book multi-day passes (3+ days) for better value. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers and carry sunscreen — alpine UV is intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic morning snowshoe hike on marked trails around the Bernese Oberland region. Snowshoe rental is much cheaper than ski rental (~15-20 CHF/day) and trails are free to use. Head toward a viewpoint overlooking the valley — trails near Grindelwald or First offer spectacular panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harder Kulm viewpoint above Interlaken via the funicular railway (round trip ~32 CHF, or check for discount passes). Enjoy sweeping views of Lake Thun, Lake Brienz, and the Bernese Alps. Alternatively, explore the free winter walking paths along the valley floor near Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Back in the village, visit a local bar or après-ski spot for one drink and soak in the mountain atmosphere. Many places offer happy hour between 4-6 PM.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket staples — muesli, milk, banana, and instant coffee prepared in-room if kitchen facilities are available (~4-6 CHF).
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and bread rolls from the supermarket to enjoy at a scenic viewpoint during your snowshoe hike (~6-10 CHF).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice meal in the accommodation kitchen if available (~5-8 CHF), or opt for a Döner kebab or supermarket hot food counter (~10-15 CHF).

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing is one of the best budget winter activities in the Alps — trails are free and equipment is affordable. Check local tourist office for free guided snowshoe walks which are sometimes offered. The Harder Kulm funicular has reduced prices after 3 PM in some seasons.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Davos for the famous Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trails experience. Davos offers over 100km of groomed Nordic and cross-country ski trails — the largest network in the Alps. Take an early train (check SBB app — journey may require 2-3 hours with connections via Chur). Cross-country ski pass is significantly cheaper than downhill (~15-25 CHF vs. 60-80 CHF).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Nordic trail network around Davos. The Davos Klosters area has trails for all levels — flat lakeside routes for beginners and more challenging forest trails for intermediate skiers. Rent cross-country skis in Davos village (~25-35 CHF/day). Stop at a trail-side warming hut for a hot chocolate.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Bernese Oberland. Arrive back in time for dinner. Rest and recover for more activities tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early supermarket breakfast before catching the train — bread, cheese slices, and juice (~5-7 CHF).
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch from Coop or Migros in Davos (sandwiches, fruit, trail mix, hot drink in thermos) to eat on the trails (~10-14 CHF).
meals.dinner: Upon return, try the accommodation's local restaurant recommendation or a simple fondue at a mid-range restaurant — look for fondue sets for one person (~22-28 CHF).

day_by_day.notes: The train journey to Davos from Bernese Oberland is long (2-3 hours each way) but scenic and covered by Swiss Travel Pass. Davos cross-country trails are free to access in some sections — check the official Davos Klosters website for current trail pass requirements. Start early to maximize time on the trails.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the downhill ski slopes for a second ski day. Focus on intermediate runs and try different lifts you haven't explored yet. Many Bernese Oberland ski areas are interconnected — explore the Grindelwald-Wengen-Mürren ski circuit if your pass covers it.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skiing, try sledding (Schlitteln) — one of Switzerland's most fun and affordable winter activities. Many resorts have dedicated sled runs, and sled rental costs only ~10-15 CHF. The Faulhorn-Bussalp sled run near Grindelwald is one of the longest natural sled runs in the Alps (15km).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the halfway point of the trip at a local fondue restaurant. Traditional cheese fondue is a must-try Swiss experience. Many restaurants offer fondue for two at ~40-50 CHF total, making it surprisingly reasonable when shared.

meals.breakfast: Hearty in-room or supermarket breakfast to fuel a full ski day — oats, eggs (if kitchen available), bread with jam (~5-8 CHF).
meals.lunch: On-mountain self-service cafeteria for a warm meal — choose soup + bread or a simple Rösti plate (~15-18 CHF). This is worth the splurge on a full ski day.
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss cheese fondue at a local restaurant. Share with a travel companion if possible to reduce cost. Pair with house wine or local beer (~20-28 CHF per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Faulhorn-Bussalp sled run requires a gondola ticket to reach the top — factor this into your budget. Sledding is best in the afternoon when the snow softens slightly. Book fondue dinner in advance on Fridays as local restaurants fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Then take a free winter walking tour of the local village. Many Swiss mountain villages have self-guided heritage walk brochures available from the tourist office at no cost. Explore historic chalets, church squares, and frozen fountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free or low-cost attraction — the Swiss Open-Air Museum at Ballenberg near Brienz offers a fascinating look at traditional Swiss architecture and rural life (entry ~20 CHF, reduced for students/youth). Alternatively, take a scenic boat ride on Lake Brienz if weather permits (~10-15 CHF). Ice skating at a local outdoor rink is another affordable option (~8-12 CHF including skate rental).
day_by_day.evening: Final big dinner of the trip — splurge slightly on a traditional Swiss Raclette dinner. Many local restaurants offer Raclette evenings on weekends with all-you-can-eat cheese melted tableside (~25-35 CHF per person). A truly memorable Swiss experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely in-room breakfast — pick up fresh croissants from a local bakery as a treat (~3-5 CHF each).
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic lunch with Swiss specialties — local cheese (Emmental or Gruyère), cured meats, dark bread, and a chocolate bar for dessert (~10-14 CHF).
meals.dinner: Traditional Raclette dinner at a local restaurant. Pair with a glass of Swiss Fendant white wine. This is your splurge meal of the trip — worth every franc (~28-38 CHF per person).

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day in Swiss ski resorts as weekend visitors arrive. If you want to ski, go early and expect longer lift queues. The Ballenberg Open-Air Museum may have limited winter hours — call ahead or check their website. Outdoor ice rinks are often free on weekday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack and check out of accommodation. Store luggage at the hotel if possible. Take one last scenic walk or snowshoe through the village and surrounding trails. Visit a local bakery for a farewell Swiss breakfast — fresh Zopf bread (braided loaf), butter, and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport or onward destination. Travel via train — use the SBB app for the most efficient route. If time allows before your train, browse local shops for affordable Swiss souvenirs: Lindt or Frey chocolate bars (~3-5 CHF), postcards (~1-2 CHF), or local cheese from a supermarket to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or travel to next destination. Reflect on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final Swiss bakery breakfast — Zopf bread, butter, jam, and a café crème (Swiss-style coffee) at a local café (~8-12 CHF). A perfect farewell to Switzerland.
meals.lunch: Airport or train station meal — Migros or Coop at the station offers the most affordable options (~10-15 CHF). Avoid airport restaurants which charge premium prices.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with your accommodation. Swiss trains to major airports run frequently and are reliable — no need to arrive excessively early. Leave at least 2 hours before your flight for international departures. Declare any cheese or meat products if flying internationally outside the EU/Schengen area.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport, clear customs, and transfer to Bernese Oberland Boutique Stay (approximately 1.5–2 hours by train via Interlaken Ost). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the village to get your bearings, spot the surrounding peaks, and locate key amenities like ski rental shops and the train station.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel, review your ski gear needs, and arrange equipment rental for the following morning at a local ski shop. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel or a nearby mountain restaurant.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or train station — grab a sandwich or soup from a station kiosk (CHF 10–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy local Bernese restaurant such as a traditional Stübli — try Rösti with smoked sausage or a cheese fondue for CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or regional Bernese Oberland Pass at the airport or train station — it will save significantly on rail and lift costs throughout the week. Confirm ski rental bookings online tonight to avoid morning queues.

day_by_day.morning: Pick up pre-booked ski rental equipment from a local shop in Grindelwald or Wengen. Head to the Jungfrau Ski Region (Grindelwald–Wengen–Mürren) slopes for a morning ski session on well-groomed blue and red runs — ideal for warming up your ski legs after travel. The First and Männlichen areas offer stunning panoramic runs suitable for all levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the cogwheel train from Grindelwald for the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Rail & Snow Experience. Ascend to 3,454m — Europe's highest railway station — and enjoy the breathtaking Aletsch Glacier views, the Ice Palace, and the Sphinx Observatory observation deck. Allow 3–4 hours for the full experience including travel time.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the valley by early evening. Relax with a warm drink at a mountain café before heading back to the hotel. Light stretching or a sauna session if the hotel offers spa facilities.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique hotel — included or CHF 15–20 if à la carte. Fuel up well before a big ski day.
meals.lunch: Quick mountain lunch at a Jungfraujoch self-service restaurant on the summit — soup, bread, and hot chocolate for CHF 20–28.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Grindelwald restaurant — try Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte or similar for pasta, raclette, or grilled meats at CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in February. Wear warm, windproof layers as summit temperatures can drop to -15°C or below. The Good Morning Ticket (early departure) is cheaper if you want to save budget.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning dedicated to skiing in the Jungfrau Ski Region — focus on intermediate to advanced red runs around Kleine Scheidegg and Lauberhorn, home of the famous World Cup downhill course. Enjoy the iconic views of the Eiger North Face as you ski.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition day — take the scenic train journey from Grindelwald/Interlaken toward Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours via Spiez and Visp). Arrive in Zermatt — the car-free village — and check in / drop bags at a luggage locker. Explore the charming main street, browse ski shops, and spot the iconic Matterhorn from the village.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zermatt's vibrant après-ski scene along the Bahnhofstrasse. Enjoy a drink at a lively bar such as Papperla Pub or Elsie's Bar before a proper sit-down dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique hotel before checkout or a light grab-and-go from a bakery.
meals.lunch: Packed snack or quick bite at Kleine Scheidegg mountain restaurant before catching the train — CHF 15–20.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt at a mid-range restaurant such as Restaurant Whymper-Stube — try the Matterhorn lamb or Swiss cheese dishes for CHF 40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: No private cars are allowed in Zermatt — the village is served by electric taxis and horse-drawn carriages. Store your main luggage at the Bernese Oberland hotel or send it ahead via Swiss Post's luggage forwarding service (SwissRail Fly Baggage). This is a travel/transition day so keep the morning ski session light.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Zermatt Ski Resort experience — purchase or use your pre-booked full-day lift pass covering over 360km of groomed runs. Start the morning on the Klein Matterhorn sector (3,883m), the highest ski area in the Alps, for extraordinary high-altitude skiing and jaw-dropping Matterhorn views. Focus on the Glacier Paradise runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing in the Rothorn and Sunnegga Paradise sectors — enjoy the varied terrain including long cruising reds and challenging blacks. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain hut for a warm drink and the classic Zermatt atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at a slope-side bar as the lifts close. Return to the village, shower and change, then enjoy a celebratory dinner in Zermatt.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Zermatt accommodation or a local café — croissant, muesli, and coffee for CHF 12–18.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a mountain restaurant on the slopes such as Chez Vrony in Findeln — renowned for its Matterhorn views and hearty mountain cuisine — CHF 30–40 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Stockhorn or a similar Zermatt mid-range option — try raclette, fondue, or local Alpine specialties for CHF 40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buy your Zermatt lift pass online in advance for a 5–10% discount. The Klein Matterhorn gondola queues can be long — arrive at the lift station by 8:30am. Sunscreen is essential at altitude even in winter — UV exposure is intense above 3,000m.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Zermatt — optional light ski warm-up run or a snowshoe walk on one of the marked snowshoe trails around Zermatt for a gentler, scenic mountain experience. Alternatively, visit the Matterhorn Museum Zermatlantis for cultural context on the region's mountaineering history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day — depart Zermatt by train toward Davos (approximately 4 hours via Visp, Brig, and Landquart). Arrive in Davos, Europe's highest city at 1,560m, and check into your accommodation. Rest and prepare for the next day's Nordic activities.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Davos Promenade, browse the town, and enjoy a relaxed dinner. Davos has a lively but more understated atmosphere compared to Zermatt.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Zermatt before departure — full hotel breakfast or a local café for CHF 15–20.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the train or at Landquart station during the connection — grab a sandwich or warm snack for CHF 12–18.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Davos at a local restaurant such as Restaurant Gentiana or a traditional Swiss Stübli — try Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and Capuns (a local Graubünden specialty) for CHF 35–48 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Davos is in the canton of Graubünden — the local cuisine shifts to Romansh-influenced dishes. This is a longer travel day so keep energy levels in mind. Book accommodation in Davos in advance as the town hosts conferences and events frequently in February.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trails experience — explore over 100km of groomed Nordic and cross-country ski trails around Davos. Start with the classic Davos–Klosters corridor trails. Rent Nordic ski equipment from a local shop if needed. The trails are well-signposted and suitable for all abilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Nordic skiing or switch to a snowshoe trail for variety. In the mid-afternoon, head to the Davos Ice Rink (Kunsteisbahn Davos) — one of the largest natural ice rinks in Europe — for ice skating and a fun change of pace from alpine skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up with a traditional Glühwein (mulled wine) at a local bar. Enjoy a lively Saturday evening dinner in Davos with the weekend crowd.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Davos hotel or a local bakery — muesli, bread, cheese, and coffee for CHF 12–18.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or a trail-side hut lunch — try a local Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) sandwich and soup at a Nordic trail hut for CHF 18–25.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Davos mid-range restaurant — try Pizzeria Padrino or Bergrestaurant Schatzalp for hearty mountain fare at CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski passes in Davos are separate from alpine lift passes and are very affordable (CHF 15–25 per day). Saturday can be busy on trails — start early for the best experience. The Davos Ice Rink is open from approximately 09:00–21:00 with skate rental available on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — optional last ski session on the Davos–Parsenn or Jakobshorn ski area for a classic alpine farewell run. Alternatively, take a scenic cable car ride up to Weissfluhjoch for panoramic views without skiing. Pack bags and check out of accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin return journey — travel from Davos by train toward Zurich Airport (approximately 2.5 hours via Landquart). Allow extra time for luggage and airport check-in procedures. Do some last-minute Swiss chocolate or souvenir shopping at the train station or airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland — reflect on an incredible week of alpine adventure in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before checkout — make it a proper send-off meal for CHF 18–25.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Davos town center before departure or on the train — grab a Bündner pastry and coffee for CHF 10–15.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport or on the flight — budget CHF 25–40 if dining at the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Zurich Airport has excellent train connections from Davos via Landquart — the journey is scenic and comfortable. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the journey plus check-in. Swiss customs rules apply for bringing back food items — chocolate and cheese have limits for non-EU travelers. Consider sending heavy ski gear home via Swiss Post if purchased locally.

meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant — a curated 4-course alpine menu featuring raclette with truffle, venison medallions with juniper jus, and a warm chocolate fondant paired with a Valais Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is confirmed in advance. Request altitude acclimatization tips from the concierge if sensitive to elevation changes. Tip: unpack fully on Day 1 to feel settled before the active days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Rail & Snow Experience — depart from Grindelwald (approx. 20–30 min from Bernese Oberland base) on the historic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m. Marvel at the UNESCO World Heritage panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier. Explore the Ice Palace and Sphinx Observatory platform.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing excursion on the high-alpine plateau near Jungfraujoch with a certified private guide. Experience the surreal silence and pristine snowscapes above the clouds. Return by cogwheel train to Grindelwald by mid-afternoon and transfer back to the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Après-mountain relaxation at the hotel spa with a 60-minute hot stone massage (pre-book with concierge). Warm up with a private fondue experience arranged in the hotel's intimate private dining room.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss alpine breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked Zopf bread, bircher muesli, smoked salmon, soft-boiled eggs, and artisan jams with mountain honey
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Restaurant at 3,454m — hot alpine soup, rösti with mountain herbs, and warm apple strudel with vanilla cream
meals.dinner: Private fondue dinner at the boutique hotel — three-cheese blend (Gruyère, Emmental, Appenzeller) with truffle shavings, crusty bread, and a bottle of Fendant du Valais white wine

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm, windproof layers for Jungfraujoch — temperatures can reach -15°C or lower at the summit. Sunglasses and SPF50+ sunscreen are essential due to intense UV reflection off snow at altitude. Book the cogwheel train tickets in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Zermatt (approximately 2 hours from Bernese Oberland — scenic route through Valais). Begin the Zermatt Ski Resort Full-Day Pass experience — access over 360km of world-class groomed runs across all skill levels. Start with the iconic Klein Matterhorn cable car to reach 3,883m for breathtaking Matterhorn views and top-to-bottom descents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing Zermatt's legendary red and black runs on the Italian-Swiss border, including the legendary Schwarzsee and Trockener Steg sectors. Option to hire a private ski instructor for personalized coaching on technique and off-piste introductions. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountaintop sun terrace restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zermatt village's car-free cobblestone streets by electric taxi. Browse luxury alpine boutiques and Swiss watch ateliers. Enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail at a chic hotel bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — power-packed with granola, fresh fruit, eggs benedict, and freshly squeezed juices to fuel a full ski day
meals.lunch: Lunch at Chez Vrony on the slopes above Findeln — Zermatt's most celebrated mountain restaurant. Enjoy truffle pasta, beef tartare, and a glass of Chasselas white wine with direct Matterhorn views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Zum See in Zermatt — a Michelin-recommended alpine gem offering wild mushroom risotto, venison ragù, and house-made desserts in a candlelit 16th-century farmhouse setting

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — all transport within the village uses electric vehicles or horse-drawn sleighs. Consider an overnight stay in Zermatt if the day feels rushed, or arrange a late private transfer back. Book Chez Vrony well in advance as it is extremely popular.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Freeride Off-Piste Guided Tour — private transfer to Verbier (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Join a IFMGA-certified mountain guide for a half-day off-piste freeride adventure through Verbier's legendary backcountry terrain including the famous Mont Gelé couloirs and hidden powder bowls. Full safety equipment (beacon, probe, shovel) provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Verbier village for a leisurely afternoon. Explore the vibrant après-ski scene with a warm Glühwein at an outdoor terrace bar. Optional: visit the Verbier ski museum or browse the luxury alpine boutiques along Rue de Médran. Private transfer back to Bernese Oberland by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy the outdoor heated jacuzzi under the stars with alpine panoramic views. Wind down with a curated Swiss whisky and schnapps tasting arranged by the hotel sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast box prepared by the hotel — energy bars, croissants, thermos of coffee, and fresh fruit for the early departure
meals.lunch: Post-freeride celebratory lunch at Verbier's La Vache Restaurant — renowned for its dry-aged prime beef, truffle fries, and exceptional wine cellar in a rustic-chic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's chef's table experience — an intimate 5-course tasting menu with wine pairings, featuring seasonal alpine ingredients curated by the executive chef

day_by_day.notes: Verbier off-piste is for intermediate to advanced skiers comfortable with steep, ungroomed terrain. Inform the guide of your exact skill level during briefing. Weather and avalanche conditions will be assessed by the guide on the morning — have a backup plan ready. Avalanche safety briefing is mandatory before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trails experience — private transfer to Davos (approx. 2–2.5 hours from Bernese Oberland). Explore over 100km of impeccably groomed Nordic trails through the Davos-Klosters valley. Hire premium classic or skate-ski equipment and enjoy a guided 2-hour Nordic ski tour through pristine forest and open meadow landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Davos Congress Centre area and explore the town, Europe's highest city at 1,560m. Optional: ice skating at the legendary Davos Ice Stadium — one of Europe's largest natural ice rinks. Alternatively, enjoy a horse-drawn sleigh ride through snow-covered forests arranged by the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to Bernese Oberland. Enjoy a quiet, restorative evening — optional in-room spa treatment (aromatherapy massage or alpine herb bath) before a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast with a focus on protein and slow-release carbohydrates — smoked trout, rye bread, yogurt parfait, and a double espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Davos's Restaurant Bolgenschanze — a classic Swiss mountain restaurant with panoramic valley views, serving homemade Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), rösti, and apple cake
meals.dinner: Dinner at a refined hotel restaurant in Bernese Oberland — wild mushroom risotto with aged Parmesan, pan-seared lake trout, and a Swiss Riesling-Sylvaner pairing

day_by_day.notes: Nordic skiing is an excellent active recovery option after the intense freeride day. Davos is also famous for its toboggan run at Schatzalp — a fun optional add-on in the afternoon. Bring sunglasses and lip balm as reflected UV on flat Nordic terrain can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: St. Moritz Snowkiting & Ice Activities on Lake St. Moritz — private luxury transfer to St. Moritz (approx. 2.5–3 hours). Begin with a 2-hour certified snowkiting lesson on the frozen Lake St. Moritz with a professional instructor. Experience the exhilarating sensation of being propelled across the ice by a power kite — a truly unique winter sport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to ice activities — enjoy a private curling session on Lake St. Moritz followed by a leisurely ice skating session on the natural frozen lake. Explore the glamorous St. Moritz village with its world-renowned luxury boutiques (Cartier, Bulgari, Hermès) and iconic Badrutt's Palace Hotel lobby.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory penultimate evening dinner in St. Moritz before returning to Bernese Oberland. Option to extend the stay in St. Moritz for the evening or return by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast at the hotel before departure — smoked salmon blinis, fresh berries, warm croissants, and a glass of Ruinart Blanc de Blancs
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hanselmann Café & Konditorei in St. Moritz — a legendary institution since 1894 offering Engadiner walnut tart, truffle scrambled eggs, and premium hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Badrutt's Palace Hotel's La Diala Restaurant, St. Moritz — an ultra-premium dining experience featuring Wagyu beef, black truffle risotto, and an extensive Grand Cru Burgundy wine list in iconic surroundings

day_by_day.notes: Snowkiting requires no prior experience — the lesson is beginner-friendly but physically engaging. Dress in windproof and waterproof layers as the lake is fully exposed to wind. St. Moritz on Saturday evenings can be extremely lively — book La Diala well in advance. The Cresta Run and Polo on Snow events may be happening in February — check the local events calendar.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the hotel. Take a final scenic walk or snowshoe through the immediate surroundings of the Bernese Oberland property, soaking in the last alpine vistas. Optional: visit a local Swiss watch or luxury goods boutique for last-minute premium souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hotel checkout with concierge-assisted luggage handling. Private chauffeured transfer to the airport or onward destination. En route, stop at a renowned Swiss chocolatier (e.g., Läderach or Sprüngli) to purchase artisan chocolate gifts — a quintessential Swiss farewell ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or onward travel. If the flight is late evening, arrange a VIP airport lounge experience for a comfortable, premium send-off.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — full Swiss spread with freshly baked pastries, artisan cheeses, cold cuts, eggs to order, fresh juices, and a final cup of Swiss mountain herbal tea
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a charming village café near the hotel — Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef), fresh salad, crusty bread, and a glass of sparkling Chasselas
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or onward destination (arrange in-flight premium dining if applicable)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours for airport transfer and check-in. Confirm private transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Pack ski equipment carefully or arrange professional ski bag shipping through the hotel. Ensure all valuables, Swiss purchases, and duty-free items are organized before departure. Request a printed or digital copy of all receipts for tax refund (VAT refund available for non-EU travelers on purchases over CHF 300).
